curated.instructions: omr/instructions/9394-1-2.pdf (jet book 1, steps 1-58) and omr/instructions/9394-1-1.pdf (jet book 2, steps 59-97; page 55 shows every function); omr/instructions/9394-1-3.pdf builds the alternate model

functions.does: Turning the round exhaust nozzle at the tail sweeps both wings back and forward together: the nozzle's 24-tooth gear turns a small gear on an axle with a worm, the worm turns a 24-tooth gear whose two gears drive a pair of racks along the fuselage, and the racks' cross axle pushes a link to each wing, which pivots near the wing root.
functions.source: book: book 1 page 65 (the nozzle turned and the racks sliding forward); book 2 page 55 (bottom left: the nozzle turning and the wings swinging)

functions.does: The smooth grey axle joiner low on the fuselage's left side raises and lowers the landing gear: it turns a worm, which turns a small gear on a long axle along the belly, and knob gears at its ends swing the nose leg and, through a cross axle, the two main legs.
functions.source: book: book 2 pages 11-14 (main gear legs, the box shows them turning) and step 68; book 2 page 55 (top right: the knob turning and the three legs swinging)

functions.does: The black gear on the spine behind the cockpit opens the canopy: it turns a worm, which turns a small gear whose two arms push a long beam forward, tilting the canopy up on its hinge at the back of the cockpit.
functions.source: book: book 2 page 33 (arrows show the knob turning and the canopy front lifting) and page 55 (bottom right)

functions.does: Moving the control stick in the cockpit forward and back tilts the two tailplanes: rods along the fuselage carry the stick's movement to a crank on the tailplanes' common axle.
functions.source: book: book 2 page 55 (top left: arrows at the stick and on both tailplanes); inferred: which rods carry it

functions.does: The three landing gear wheels roll freely.
